extracted.intended_audience: self-regulatory organizations (exchanges) filing rule/fee changes, their counsel, market participants, and SEC staff reviewing fee filings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and narrative supporting a Securities Exchange Act Section 19(b)(1)/Rule 19b-4 filing to amend an exchange fee schedule (connectivity and port fees). Describes the statutory standards, Staff Guidance expectations, cost- and competition-based justification approaches, required disclosures, and specific fee schedule drafting/implementation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with Section 6(b) of the Act
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed fees must be consistent with section 6(b) of the Exchange Act, and in particular with sections 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, filings should show that fees 'provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges' (6(b)(4)) and 'promote just and equitable principles of trade, remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system' (6(b)(5)). Filings should explain how the proposed fees are not unfairly discriminatory and do not create an undue burden on competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonableness of the fee
rubrics_metrics.description: A fee must be reasonable — not excessive or resulting in supra-competitive profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonableness can be shown via market-based arguments (fees constrained by significant competitive forces) or via a cost-based justification demonstrating that fees recover costs with reasonable mark-up. Filings should provide evidence supporting that the fee is fair and reasonable and will not result in excessive pricing or supra-competitive profit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable allocation / no unfair discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees must be equitably allocated among Members and other persons using the facility and must not be unfairly discriminatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how fee structure treats similarly situated participants consistently and why any differentiated treatment is justified. Cite 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5) obligations and provide evidence that the fee will not permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers and dealers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not an undue burden on competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed fees must not create an undue burden on competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show that fees will not materially impair competition among market participants or between exchanges (e.g., by preventing non-legacy exchanges from competing on transaction fees or investing in infrastructure). Discuss competitive effects and provide supporting data or rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market-based test: demonstrate fees constrained by significant competitive forces
rubrics_metrics.description: As an initial step, staff considers whether the fee is constrained by significant competitive forces (market-based justification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If asserting a market-based constraint, supply evidence of competitive pressures (e.g., alternative venues, ability of participants to choose not to access). Cite Staff Guidance language that 'as an initial step in assessing the reasonableness of a fee, staff considers whether the fee is constrained by significant competitive forces.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-based justification (alternative to market-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a market-based constraint is not asserted or is insufficient, provide a cost-based discussion to show consistency with the Exchange Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff Guidance requires 'specific information, including quantitative information' to support cost recovery claims. Filings should include comprehensive cost and revenue data, cost allocations, and explanation of methodology; the Exchange provides cost analyses, projected margins, and how fees relate to costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive revenue and cost data and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide full cost and revenue analysis supporting the fee, including quantification of costs, allocation bases, and projected profit margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include descriptions of expenses (e.g., R&D, network monitoring, internal expenses), aggregated cost totals, how costs were computed, revenue projections, and margin calculations; update cost analysis as strategic initiatives and costs change. Address why costs justify the proposed fee levels and show that margins are not excessive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost allocation methodology among affiliated markets
rubrics_metrics.description: When allocating shared costs among affiliated exchanges/markets, explain methodology and ensure no cost is allocated more than once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detail on how shared hardware/software and personnel costs are allocated among affiliated markets, explain differences in allocations between affiliates, and justify why allocations may differ from similar proposals by affiliates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and disclosure standards (meet or exceed Staff Guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filings should meet high standards of transparency to show why a fee is reasonable, equitably allocated, and not unfairly discriminatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given the Staff Guidance and precedent (BOX Order etc.), exchanges should provide detailed disclosures (quantitative and qualitative) sufficient to allow Staff and the Commission to assess reasonableness. The filing notes frustration when Staff find provided detail insufficient; exchanges may request clarity from Staff on required data and acceptable margins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with precedent (BOX Order) and Staff Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that the proposed fees comply with applicable Commission orders and Staff Guidance (including BOX Order and subsequent Staff Guidance on fee filings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how the submission addresses issues raised in precedent disapprovals and follows Staff Guidance recommendations (e.g., considering competition and/or providing cost-based analysis). Cite relevant release numbers and explain how the filing satisfies those precedents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a record sufficient for Commission review
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a record and written explanations sufficient to enable the Commission to perform its review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Remand Order/Staff Guidance direction to 'develop a record' — explain conclusions based on that record in written form so the Commission can evaluate the rationale for the fee change. Include factual support, analysis, and citations to comparable fee schedules and market data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify fee mechanics and implementation details (fees, pro-ration, effective dates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee filings must specify the precise fee amounts, how they are assessed (per month, per port, per matching engine), pro-ration rules when changes occur mid-month, and implementation/effective dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: pro-rate fees based on number of trading days a member is credentialed divided by trading days in the month; state whether changes are immediately effective and include any transition or grandfathering provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define key terms and include Definitions section
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee Schedule should include clear definitions for terms used (e.g., 'Matching Engine', 'Limited Service MEI Port', 'Full Service MEI Port').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions should explain scope and mechanics (e.g., what a matching engine processes, per-root symbol assignment), and identify caps or limits tied to definitions (e.g., number of free ports per matching engine). Make ministerial changes or clarifications where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify caps, tiers, and structure of fee offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: If the fee schedule includes tiered structures or caps (e.g., number of free ports, limits on additional ports), state them clearly and quantitatively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the number of free ports (e.g., first four free), the monthly fee for additional ports (e.g., $420 for fifth and above), and any cap (e.g., limited to fourteen Limited Service MEI Ports per Matching Engine). Explain rationale for tiers and caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify competitive effects: parity and pro-competitive rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the proposed fees affect competition among exchanges and promote competition (e.g., ensure parity with legacy exchanges, enable investments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue how fee changes facilitate parity with legacy exchanges, allow non-legacy exchanges to invest and compete, and/or permit lowering transaction fees using non-transaction revenue; support claims with comparative revenue data from legacy exchanges where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and compliance with SEC rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain records and comply with applicable SEC recordkeeping rules (e.g., 17 CFR 240.17a-1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite recordkeeping obligations and ensure documentation supporting cost and revenue analysis is retained and available for inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of subscriber behavior and revenue sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether customers will continue subscribing at new fee levels and consider alternative scenarios if subscribers drop service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Exchange may deem such an analysis less useful when amending existing fees (versus adopting a new fee), precedent (IEX) includes projections of customer retention vs. attrition; include such analysis when relevant to revenue projections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite comparative fees and precedents
rubrics_metrics.description: Support fee proposals with comparisons to other exchanges' pricing and rule filings, and cite relevant Commission releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide links or citations to other exchanges' price lists (e.g., Nasdaq, NYSE) and SEC release numbers to contextualize fee levels and support assertions about parity or competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of double-counting and clear separation of shared vs. specific costs
rubrics_metrics.description: When attributing costs to a particular fee, ensure shared costs are not double-counted and separate costs that specifically support the service from general corporate costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain allocation bases (e.g., hardware/software usage, matching engine counts), include granularity where possible, and note differences from peers' allocation approaches (e.g., director cost allocations).
